title: Read the check-in date a guest typed

blocks.text: The hotel's booking form takes the check-in date as typed text. Front-desk staff report guests who arrive on a day the hotel has no booking for: one typed `2025-09-31` and was booked for 1 October, another pasted `2025-10-12 15:00` from an email. A partner site that sends `2025-7-4` has asked whether that format is supported; the answer is no, and the form should say so.

Finish `checkInDate(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/CheckInForm.java`. It returns the date when the field holds exactly one real date written as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for anything else, so that `review(...)` asks the guest again. About five lines.

cases.says: a well-formed date is read as that date, and text that is no date at all is refused
a day that does not exist, such as the 31st of a 30-day month, is refused rather than moved to the next month
a date followed by more text is refused
a month or day typed without its leading zero is refused

origin.section: Parsing Is Lenient by Default, and Strict Mode Still Ignores What Follows the Date

concepts: SimpleDateFormat parses leniently by default, turning an impossible date into a real one.
Even with setLenient(false), SimpleDateFormat.parse(String) ignores text after the date and does not enforce the pattern's widths; LocalDate.parse reads and validates the whole text.
